steps.text: Sonority means a material makes a clear ringing sound when struck. Let's test which materials are sonorous.
Tap a metal object to strike it.
Hear that? A clear ringing sound that sustains — metals are sonorous. That's why bells and gongs are made of metal.
Now strike a non-metal object — it makes a dull thud with no ring. Metals are sonorous, non-metals are not.

coach.mission: Strike a metal and a non-metal and listen to the difference.
whenStuck: Tap an object to strike it and listen.
Strike a metal, then a non-metal, and compare the sound.
whenWrong: Metals ring (sonorous); non-metals make a dull thud.
A dull sound means it's a non-metal — not sonorous.
whenCorrect: Right — the metal rang clearly, so it's sonorous.
Good — the non-metal only thudded because it isn't sonorous.
coach.done: You've heard that metals are sonorous and non-metals are not. Test more objects, or move on when you're ready.
